segments.text: But now, I just want them to feel good so that they want to come again.

segments.speaker: Gloria Marin
segments.text: [SPEAKING SPANISH]

segments.speaker: Lizzie Presser
segments.text: So these days, that's Gloria's entire strategy. She tries to play it cool when she's on the phone with them. She doesn't want to sound needy or talk about how hard things are for her.

segments.speaker: Lizzie Presser
segments.text: In the morning, back in Phoenix, Yesi put on full makeup. Brisa, the youngest kid, braided Angel's hair. The three of them packed into the car around 7:00 AM with Yesi's kids and headed south to stand on the Arizona side of the border and talk to their mom through a fence.

segments.speaker: Lizzie Presser
segments.text: In Nogales, Gloria finished cooking and then sat on her bed, watching the clock, still unaware that her kids weren't planning to cross over. When it hit 10:00 AM, Gloria left her house, got in her car, and started driving to the border to pick them up, 10 minutes away.

segments.speaker: Lizzie Presser
segments.text: [PHONE RINGING]

segments.speaker: Lizzie Presser
segments.text: Suddenly, her cell phone rang.

segments.speaker: Gloria Marin
segments.text: [SPEAKING SPANISH]

segments.speaker: Lizzie Presser
segments.text: It was her kids.

segments.speaker: Gloria Marin
segments.text: [SPEAKING SPANISH]

segments.speaker: Lizzie Presser
segments.text: Gloria's saying, are you guys coming?

segments.speaker: Gloria Marin
segments.text: [SPEAKING SPANISH]

segments.speaker: Lizzie Presser
segments.text: Wait, you're there? I'm on my way.

segments.speaker: Gloria Marin
segments.text: OK, mijo, I love you.

segments.speaker: Lizzie Presser
segments.text: Her kids had all crossed. I don't think it was because I was with them recording. They'd had a massive change of heart. Brisa, the youngest, had been telling her siblings that Gloria was doing fine, and they needed to chill out and stop making such a big deal out of visiting her house.

segments.speaker: Lizzie Presser
segments.text: And so when they got to the border, the siblings didn't talk about it. Nobody said anything. Angel looked down and saw his feet walking across the border. They pushed through a metal gate. Suddenly, they were in Mexico. Gloria pulled up and honked.

segments.speaker: Lizzie Presser
segments.text: Yesi, it's your first time here in three years.

segments.speaker: Yesi Marin
segments.text: I know. It's been a while.

segments.speaker: Lizzie Presser
segments.text: Yesi went to hug her. She told her mom that her hair smelled good. Everyone kissed each other and piled into the car.

segments.speaker: Lizzie Presser
segments.text: At Gloria's house, the kids immediately sat down to start eating. They only had an hour. Angel had to get back to Phoenix for work that night.

segments.speaker: Lizzie Presser
segments.text: For all their talk about their hang ups with their mom, they got casual really fast. Yesi's bodysuit was bothering her, so she unsnapped it and let the flaps hang loose. Angel was trying to learn how to say "burp" in Spanish.

segments.speaker: Angel Marin
segments.text: Is it "eructa" or "erupta?"

segments.speaker: Gloria Marin
segments.text: Eructa.

segments.speaker: Lizzie Presser
segments.text: Gloria wasn't eating. She was just watching them. She had this dreamy smile on her face. This was the first time they'd all sat around a table together since 2010.

segments.speaker: Lizzie Presser
segments.text: After lunch, they all climbed into Gloria's bed, insisting they had food comas. But really, they just wanted an excuse to cuddle with their mom. Angel curled up. He's about 5 feet, 90 pounds. He'd insisted on wearing a baggy sweatshirt that day so he didn't look too skinny. Gloria started rubbing his head. It was like a magic trick.

segments.speaker: Angel Marin
segments.text: When my mom rubs my head and I'm sleeping, it's already over.

segments.speaker: Lizzie Presser
segments.text: Angel closed his eyes, and then it was time to leave. Yesi and her kids stayed behind with Gloria, but just for three extra days this time. They talked again about living together in Mexico.

segments.speaker: Lizzie Presser
segments.text: Yesi told her she'd move down there in a month or so. She'd buy Gloria a plot of land with a small house, just big enough for the whole family. Yesi told me it made them both happy, just saying all those things, even though she knew and her mom knew that it wasn't going to happen. And for the first time, that was OK.
